title: The First Form of Boredom: Becoming Bored BY Something (Gelangweiltwerden von etwas)

sections.title: The questionableness of boredom; awakening this fundamental attunement as letting it be awake, as guarding against it falling asleep
The fundamental attunement of boredom, its relation to time, and the three metaphysical questions concerning world, finitude, individuation
Interpreting boredom from that which is boring: that which holds us in limbo and leaves us empty; the questionableness of the three conventional schemata (cause-effect, psychological, transference)
Methodological directive: avoiding analysis of consciousness; interpreting boredom via passing the time (Zeitvertreib) as our immediate relation to it
Becoming bored and passing the time
Passing the time as a driving-away of boredom that drives time on
Passing the time and looking at our watch; becoming bored as being affected in a paralysing way by time as it drags
Being held in limbo (Hingehaltenheit) by time as it drags
Being left empty (Leergelassenheit) by the refusal of things, and its connection with being held in limbo

key_terms.gloss: boredom; literally 'long while' — Heidegger plays on Lange Weile (long-while) to expose boredom's structural relation to time
becoming bored BY something; the passive form naming the first, situation-bound form of boredom (a determinate boring thing)
passing the time; literally a 'driving-away of time' — our immediate everyday relation to boredom, a driving-away of boredom that drives time on
being held in limbo / to hold in limbo; the first structural moment — by time as it drags we are held fast yet given leeway, held up toward nothing in particular
being left empty / left empty; the second structural moment — the refusal of things that, though at hand, offer nothing
fundamental attunement; the disclosive mood that cannot be 'ascertained' but must be let-be-awake
releasement; the freeing of our everyday perspective from psychological and consciousness-theories, the methodological comportment required
demand / imposition; the 'almost insane demand' that we let boredom be awake rather than shake it off
melancholy; the threshold toward which obstinate boredom propels us
taken (by); in reading a boring book we are given over to it yet not taken by it; later, being taken by things is what fills emptiness
impressing / impressing-upon; the peculiar pressing of the power of time to which we are bound in becoming bored
to tarry / a while; the 'whiling' that boredom protracts — at issue in Langeweile is a Weile, a tarrying, a peculiar enduring
metaphor (μεταφορά); from Aristotle's Poetics, the transfer (metapherein) by which attunements are said to be carried from us onto things — the transference schema Heidegger contests
moment of vision; not yet thematized here but the temporal rupture toward which the whole boredom analysis is ordered (named in later forms)

claims.text: Awakening a fundamental attunement does not mean making it awake in the first place but letting it be awake, guarding against it falling asleep; everyday passing-the-time is precisely the effort to make boredom fall asleep.
The demand not to let boredom fall asleep is an 'almost insane demand' (Zumutung) opposed to all natural everyday comportment, which exists to ward off boredom.

Boredom (Langeweile) shows in the German word an obvious relation to time, a feeling of time; the question of boredom thereby leads to the problem of time, which is in turn the root of the three questions of world, finitude, and individuation.

The interpretation begins not from boredom but from boringness (Boringness): boredom is not simply an inner spiritual experience but sits outside, seated in what is boring, and creeps into us from outside.

The cause-effect schema must be disregarded: the book is not the outer cause nor the resulting boredom the inner effect; the boring thing must make itself felt not as inducing cause but as that which attunes us.

The transference schema (Aristotle's metaphor) is questionable: if what is 'transferred' already pertains to the thing itself, then we are not transferring but apprehending it from the things themselves.

That which is boring is that which holds us in limbo (hingehalten) and yet leaves us empty (leer gelassen): wearisome = it does not rivet us, we are held in limbo; tedious = it does not engross us, we are left empty.
Boredom, and ultimately every attunement, is a hybrid — partly objective, partly subjective; the attunement plays around the thing outside without our transferring anything onto it.

Methodological directive: we must not make boredom an object swimming in the stream of consciousness; we must avoid analysis of consciousness and preserve the immediacy of everyday Dasein, which requires releasement (Gelassenheit) of our everyday perspective.

It is precisely in passing the time (Zeitvertreib) that we first gain the correct orientation to encounter boredom undisguised, because boredom asserts itself precisely where we oppose it; we must consider boredom in the way we move within it.
Passing the time is a driving-away of boredom that drives time on (a 'Zeit antreibendes Wegtreiben der Langeweile'); we do not chase time away but drive it on so that it passes.
Boredom is not a waiting, nor an impatience, nor ill humour; waiting and impatience may surround boredom but never constitute it.
Looking at our watch is not itself a way of passing the time but a sign that passing-the-time is failing and that we are becoming increasingly bored; it is a helpless gesture.
What oppresses us is not that time is too long or merely slow but that it is too slow: we fight against the dragging (vacillating, paralysing) of time; the measurable stretch plays no role.

Becoming bored is a peculiar being affected in a paralysing way by time as it drags and by time in general — an oppression rooted in the enigmatic, transformable essence of time and the way time temporalizes itself.
We must stick with boredom and not collapse it into the problem of time, so that through boredom's essence we may glimpse the concealed essence of time and the connection between the two.

Being held in limbo by time as it drags is oppressive even though dragging holds back: time holds us toward nothing in particular over this particular interval (between arrival and the train's departure); passing-the-time betrays the place to which time holds us.
To leave empty means to be something at hand that offers nothing; things leave us empty precisely because they are at hand yet refuse themselves — leaving in peace is a leaving empty.
The station refuses itself as a station because the train is not yet there; disappointment is not boredom — where disappointed we withdraw, but here we stay and are held in limbo.

Being left empty and being held in limbo are not pieced together but structurally interwoven; being held in limbo by time appears the all-embracing and primarily determinative moment — the dragging of time forces things to refuse themselves.

Boredom is possible only because each thing has its time; if things did not have their time there would be no boredom — the as-yet-obscure relation of dragging time to self-refusing things is the question of what time itself is.

interlocutors.name: Aristotle
interlocutors.role: Source of the 'metaphor' (μεταφορά) doctrine from the Poetics, invoked as the classical warrant for the transference schema that Heidegger finds questionable

interlocutors.name: Novalis (implicit)
interlocutors.role: The 'philosophizing as homesickness' motif recalled ('Homesickness — philosophizing, we heard somewhere'); boredom as homesickness via Alemannic 'long-time' = 'homesick'

interlocutors.name: Idealist philosophy (generic)
interlocutors.role: Holder of the 'old truth' that properties are representations transferred by subjects onto objects — the position whose self-evidence Heidegger suspends
